title: Single Person's AI Stack Breached 20 Japanese Firms and 7 Korean Banks

tickers.name: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A Common Stock

summary:
A sophisticated combination of autonomous AI agents may have enabled one attacker to infiltrate dozens of Asian corporate and financial networks, according to a report from CrowdStrike. The hacker allegedly used a toolchain consisting of the ARTEX penetration agent alongside DeepSeek v4.1-Flash, GLM-5.3, Grok 4.6, and Claude Code to automate breaches against about 20 Japanese companies and seven South Korean banks.

The security firm Ierae found that the server used for the Japanese campaign concentrated its attacks on a single industry, affecting nine of the targeted firms. The campaign followed a series of breaches at South Korean financial institutions that began in late September. CrowdStrike tied the operation to a likely Chinese-speaking, financially motivated actor who repurposed the ARTEX tool, originally built for authorized network defense, to conduct cross-border attacks.

selectedTweets.text:
Bloomberg: An open-source agent built for authorised penetration testing became the shared engine of breach campaigns in both South Korea and Japan within weeks.

The Japanese attack server Ierae examined targeted about 20 companies almost exclusively in Japan, and 9 of them worked in the same industry.

In South Korea, CrowdStrike tied the tool to a likely Chinese-speaking, financially motivated actor who ran it mainly on DeepSeek v4.1-flash against financial firms from late September.
